items.note: Marktspiegel 11.12.2019 (updated 12.12.2019): Verkehrsausschuss 'beschlossen, Weinmarkt, Bergstraße und Maxbrücke für den Autoverkehr zu sperren'; Weinmarkt 'testweise'; CSU quote about missing 'Gesamtkonzept Altstadt' confirmed. Off: the exemptions are stated for the Maxbrücke only and are tourist buses (Touristenbusse), emergency vehicles and taxis, not buses generally; page speaks of cutting/interrupting the Bergstraße for car traffic, not specifically 'through traffic'.
items.corrected_text: Nürnberg's traffic committee decided to close the Weinmarkt (on a trial basis), the Bergstraße and the Maxbrücke to car traffic in the Altstadt; tourist buses, emergency vehicles and taxis may still cross the Maxbrücke. The local CSU criticised the plan for lacking an overall Altstadt concept.

items.note: Page confirms 27.01.2021, 'großer parteiübergreifender Mehrheit', 61% to about 68% by 2030, and the parking wording (Neuordnung des Parkens zugunsten Zufußgehende und Grün; Quartiersgaragen with Parkraumbewirtschaftung and fewer spaces in public space). Off: it was adopted by the council's Ferienausschuss (holiday committee), not the full city council.
items.corrected_text: The city council's holiday committee (Ferienausschuss) adopted the 'Mobilitätsbeschluss für Nürnberg' with a broad cross-party majority, targeting a rise in the share of trips on foot, by bike and by public transport from 61% to about 68% by 2030. Its parking approach is to reorganise parking in favour of pedestrians and greenery, with neighbourhood garages under parking management and fewer spaces in public space.

items.note: PDF text extracted with pypdf (printed 05-2021). Confirms Verkehrsausschuss decision, all previously free spaces become 'Mischprinzip' spaces, permit holders unlimited, others pay within signed max duration, regulation time 8:00-22:00, goals incl. more use of Innenstadtparkhäuser by Dauerparker and fewer spaces in the Altstadt, B and C already switched, A from August 2021, all areas by end of 2021. PDF metadata title: 'Umstellung der Parkraumbewirtschaftung in der Nürnberger Altstadt'.

Marktspiegel article dated 10.03.2022, byline '(pm/nf)' indicating a press release. Confirms A-C in 2021, D (south of Pegnitz) from December 2021, completion end of February 2022, paid parking for all up to four hours max, permit holders free and unlimited.
nordbayern 22.02.2025: ministry keeps 30.70 euro cap, had shelved the new regulation in 2023; Munich, Nürnberg, Regensburg and Erlangen argued for a higher cap.

Confirms closure June 2023, city purchase October 2024, 220-space garage on Breite Gasse, temporary uses since September 2025, council decision January 2026 to start a structured selection process. Off: 'summer 2028' is how long anchor tenant Wöhrl uses the building, not the duration of the selection process or the long-term use.
items.corrected_text: The Galeria Kaufhof store on Königstraße closed in June 2023 and the city bought the building, which has a 220-space garage on Breite Gasse, in October 2024. Temporary uses began in September 2025, anchor tenant Wöhrl is to use the building until summer 2028, and in January 2026 the council decided to start a structured selection process for the site's long-term development.

items.note: Press release 29.11.2024 confirms reopening from 29 Nov 2024, closed since June 2023, 220 spaces, Goldbeck Parking Services on behalf of the city, barrier-free number-plate recognition, opening tariff 5 euros per 24 h for short-stay parkers, timed with the Christkindlesmarkt. Off: payment is described as cashless at machines (enter plate), not 'card-only'; access is via both Kornmarkt and Frauengasse; the 5-euro rate is an opening tariff.
items.corrected_text: The former Kaufhof garage on Frauengasse (access via Kornmarkt and Frauengasse), closed since June 2023, reopened on 29 November 2024 with 220 spaces, run by Goldbeck Parking Services for the city. It uses barrier-free number-plate recognition with cashless pay machines, and the opening tariff for short-stay parkers is 5 euros per 24 hours.

items.note: Konii 11.12.2024 (teaser; full article behind login, source HIH Invest): HIH Invest won PARK ONE as new operator of the garage under Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz, 268 spaces incl. EV charging, lease start after renovation in spring 2025. The accessible page does not state that HIH Invest is the owner.
items.corrected_text: HIH Invest signed PARK ONE as the new operator of the underground garage below Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz (268 spaces, including EV charging), with the lease due to start after renovation work finishes in spring 2025.

items.note: ZfK 27.07.2021 confirms Sandreuth, 338 spaces, 128 charge points, reservation via app 'AppStellen', camera reads plate and display assigns a space, network with seven other garages in Nürnberg and Fürth, prices lowered in participating outer garages when centre pollution rises. Off: the page does not describe Sandreuth as outside the centre (only 'Stadtteil Sandreuth').
items.corrected_text: N-ERGIE opened its 'Parkhaus der Zukunft' on its site in the Sandreuth district with 338 spaces and 128 EV charge points. Spaces can be reserved by app and a display assigns a space after a camera reads the number plate; it works with seven other Nürnberg and Fürth garages, where prices in participating outer garages are lowered when city-centre air pollution is high.

items.note: ZfK 29.03.2019: six Nürnberg and four Fürth garages outside the city centres, 3,100 sensors, 370 charge points planned, 3.8m euro from the federal transport ministry's Sofortprogramm Saubere Luft, prices adapting to traffic and air pollution, completion with platform launch planned by end of 2020. Kept as a plan.
N-ERGIE magazine 28.02.2024: Herrnhütte 36, Langwasser-Süd 32, Am Wegfeld 26 charge points; parking free with valid public-transport ticket.

Page 'Parken in Nürnberg' (undated): 'über 5.300 Plätze' in 19 city-centre garages, updated every 15 minutes; fees 'innerhalb der Altstadt sowie im nahen Umfeld in der Regel' 2.50 euros, outside 2 euros per hour; PayByPhone on all spaces. Off: 'over' 5,300 not 'about'; the 2.50 rate applies to the Altstadt and its immediate surroundings as a rule, not strictly inside the walls.
items.corrected_text: The city's parking page describes a guidance system covering over 5,300 spaces in 19 city-centre garages, updated every 15 minutes. It puts on-street fees at usually 2.50 euros an hour in the Altstadt and its immediate surroundings and 2 euros an hour elsewhere, and says all spaces can be paid with the PayByPhone app.

items.note: inFranken article dated 20.11.2021: Söder announced on 19.11.2021 that all Christmas markets in Bavaria are banned due to the Corona situation; mayor König: market cannot take place 'im zweiten Jahr in Folge'. Fact date 2021-11-19 is fine.
Press release 23.12.2024: closes 24 December at 14:00; the city 'rechnet mit' about two million visitors, i.e. an expected/estimated figure issued before the market ended, not a reported count.
items.corrected_text: Ahead of the 2024 Christkindlesmarkt closing on 24 December, the city said it expected about two million visitors.

items.note: VAG Geschäftsbericht 2024 (PDF via curl/pypdf): more than 160m passengers (prev. 154m), a new record; 281,000 subscriptions of which 259,000 Deutschlandtickets. Off: the 'more than 180% vs April 2023' refers to subscription demand overall, not to the Deutschlandticket count.
items.corrected_text: VAG, the Nürnberg transport operator, carried a record of more than 160 million passengers in 2024, up from 154 million in 2023. Subscriptions reached 281,000, including 259,000 Deutschlandtickets, which VAG put at more than 180% above April 2023, the last month before the ticket was introduced.

items.note: Press release 29.01.2026: laser counting; Königstraße ~14m (+2.6%), Karolinenstraße ~13.2m (+3%), Ludwigsplatz ~8m (+6.9%), Breite Gasse ~6.6m despite ongoing redesign works. Title on page is 'Nachrichten aus dem Rathaus: Passantenfrequenz 2025: Positive Entwicklung in der Innenstadt'.
items.corrected_title: Nachrichten aus dem Rathaus: Passantenfrequenz 2025: Positive Entwicklung in der Innenstadt

corrected_summary: In December 2019 Nürnberg's traffic committee decided to close the Weinmarkt (as a trial), the Bergstraße and the Maxbrücke to car traffic, and in January 2021 a council committee adopted a Mobilitätsbeschluss that plans fewer street spaces in favour of pedestrians and greenery; by February 2022 all formerly free on-street spaces in the Altstadt had become paid, time-limited spaces for non-residents. The former Kaufhof garage, closed since June 2023, reopened in November 2024 on behalf of the city, run by Goldbeck with number-plate recognition. The Christkindlesmarkt was cancelled in 2020 and 2021 and the city expected about two million visitors in 2024, VAG reported a record of more than 160 million passengers in 2024, and pedestrian counts on the main shopping streets rose in 2025.
